title: In 27 mouse thalamic nuclei, T-type calcium channel expression did not explain burst firing but cortical input share did; brain-wide, Kv3.1 expression tracked spike duration
abstract: Question: earlier work found that the cortical share of afferent input (S) predicts burst firing across 27 mouse thalamic nuclei, and that wiring and cell-type mix both predict regional spiking. Does a specific molecular mechanism explain these links? Low-threshold bursts need T-type Ca2+ channels (Cacna1g/h/i) and brief spikes need Kv3 channels (Kcnc1/2). Data: IBL Brain-Wide Map phenotypes (62,049 units, 182 regions; burst fraction of 27 nuclei), regional gene expression from Allen Brain Cell Atlas 10x cluster means weighted by the MERFISH cluster mix (1.92 million neurons; replication brain 0.99 million), Allen ISH, Knox 2019 connectome. The plan was frozen before testing; inference used spatial surrogate maps and all 21,309 expressed genes as a reference. Results: T-channel expression did not predict thalamic bursts (rho 0.25, surrogate p = 0.12; ISH rho 0.01). Most dorsal nuclei express T channels at the same high level. S kept its link after control of T-channel expression (partial rho 0.78, p < 0.001) and of T-channel expression plus midline distance (0.49, p = 0.009), in both MERFISH brains and with ISH. Brain-wide, the T-channel score went with the burst index (rho 0.29, 98th gene percentile) but not beyond spatial smoothness (p = 0.18). The pre-set Kv3 sum did not predict spike duration (rho -0.08). A pre-set double-dissociation contrast was positive, but only because T-channel expression went with longer spikes; we do not count it as support. Post hoc, Kcnc1 alone tracked spike duration (rho -0.63, surrogate p = 0.001; replication -0.54) and firing rate (0.66). Inside thalamic nuclei, local T-channel expression had a small, non-specific link with unit bursts. Exploratory: S beat 99.8% of single-gene maps, but a cross-validated cell-type-mix model predicted bursts equally well (0.75). Conclusion: the thalamic burst gradient is not a gradient of T-channel transcript; wiring, position and cell-type mix stay confounded. Limitations: correlational, region-level, one animal per atlas, transcript is not channel function, 27 nuclei, Kcnc1 is post hoc.

(d) Rho of all 21,276 single-gene maps with burst fraction; lines show CaT, Cacna1g, S and the cross-validated cell-type-mix model.

Brain-wide, 182 regions. (a) T-channel score against ACG burst index. (b) Kcnc1 score against spike duration (post hoc). (c) Distribution of single-gene rho for burst index and duration, with the tested scores. (d) Observed rho (dot) against the 95% range of 1,000 spatial surrogate maps (bar).

Unit level inside thalamic nuclei: standardized beta of local MERFISH gene scores (200 um) and of midline distance on the unit ACG burst index, with nucleus fixed effects and 95% session-bootstrap intervals.
